dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi there! I'm looking to buy a book today. I love romance novels, so I'm hoping you can recommend something good in that genre. Could you tell me what romance books you have available?
dialogue.agent:
Great, I've found several books that relate to romance! Here are some options for you:

1. **"PS I Love You (Sweet Dreams Series #1)"** - $199.00 - ⭐ 5.0 (4 reviews) - A romance classic from the Sweet Dreams series
2. **"Transcending Fire"** - $23.95 - ⭐ 5.0 (1 review) - A steamy romance with supernatural elements
3. **"An Amish Deception: An Amish Romance Inspired by a Beloved Bible Story"** - $12.99 - ⭐ 5.0 (1 review) - An Amish romance
4. **"To Sleep Gently"** - $4.99 - ⭐ 4.9 (18 reviews) - Highly rated with many reviews
5. **"Untamed"** - $6.14 - ⭐ 5.0 (1 review)

What kind of budget are you working with? Also, do you have any other preferences — like do you prefer contemporary romance, historical romance, something steamy, or sweet and clean? And are customer ratings and reviews important to you?

products.title: Ausgrenor: The first novel in the Raising Up Pharaoh series
products.description: About the Author R. E. J. Burke is a former U. S. Marine, graduate of the University of Maryland and Yale Graduate School, aeronautical engineer, shipbuilder, banker, entrepreneur, author, and Christian speaker. His passion is the archaeology of the Chalcolithic and early Bronze Age in Western Asia, Eastern Europe, and Northeastern Africa, which led to his writing the six-novel Raising Up Pharaoh epic. Having lived in Asia, South America, the U.S. Midwest and on both coasts, he and his wife, Nancy, now live on the bluffs by the Potomac River in Shepherdstown, West Virginia. They have four adult children and six grandchildren, for whom they are very thankful. His favorite authors are Patrick O'Brian, J. R. R. Tolkien, Charles Dickens, Bernard Cornwell, C. S. Lewis, and Stephen R. Donaldson.

products.title: Untamed
Cupid's Curse: Legends of Astraea, Series
Helen's Orphans (Troy to Rome)
products.description: Review "The love story of Timon and Lukas offers the most joyous, tender and poignant sections of this imaginative novel. Proficient, modern prose and dialogue, enhanced by lifestyle details, make an ancient epic especially accessible. An enjoyable, inventive Trojan War tale with an intriguing final twist and a serious message." Kirkus Reviews "Tender, compelling, dazzling. History, myth, intrigue, and long-buried secrets mark this beautifully told story. Fritsch's extraordinary storytelling abilities shine as he brings to life the larger-than-life heroes and villains of the Trojan War. The skillfully evoked era and meticulously researched period details, combined with the crisp, straightforward prose and smoothly paced narrative make for a page-turning story pulsing with romance, sacrifice, conspiracies, betrayals, and battles. Lovers of Greek mythology and historical fiction won't want to miss this one." The Prairies Book Review "Fritsch crafts a detailed and immersive fiction that is charming in its minute detail. Helen's point-of-view passages give the legend charm and agency. Fritsch's new spin on a timeless tale will draw in readers with his sympathetic characterization and original inventions." BookLife Reviews "Fritsch did an amazing job creating this story. I really enjoyed reading it and did so in a single sitting. Fans of Greek mythology and ancient history will really enjoy this novel." Reader Views "Fritsch spins a complex web of secrets and revelations that keep the reader engaged throughout. His plot lines are constantly moving forward toward an inevitable collision. His ability to objectively examine alternative angles of a classical work is commendable." US Review of Books From the Author Helen's Orphans has won the gold medal in the LGBTQIA category of the 2020-2021 Reader Views Literary Awards. The novel has won a finalist award in the 2021 Book Excellence Awards. From the Back Cover Did Helen choose to run off to Troy with Paris, or did he force her togo with him? Two orphans of the Trojan War, the tragic conflict Helen'selopement or abduction precipitated, search for the answer to one of the oldest questions in history--and discover much more. About the Author Fritsch has written ten award-winning novels, mainly in the historical fiction and mystery genres. Read more

products.title: The Peacekeeper (Britannia Romanus)
products.description: Review I have loved every book written by Jess Steven Hughes, historical novels and set in Roman Britain. Where, you say? Read the First four Hughes books, once referred to as the "Sign of the Eagle" series, and find out. Now Hughes has given us a new book, the Peacekeeper. And with it, new branding for his historical adventure series begins in earnest: Henceforth called the "Britannia Romanus" series, the triumph of these earlier volumes is about to be eclipsed with the publication of the Peacekeeper, #5 in this story but a magnificent stand-alone read as well. Why do I recommend the Britannia Romanus series? Because it's that good, good enough to recommend without reservation. Few can do what Hughes does, mixing genres to bring us books that open doors into worlds previously unknown, time after time. Hughes writes a combination of mystery, adventure, suspense and romance seldom equaled. A former Marine and police detective, real-life experience informs every sentence, every page. Those characters breathe and suffer and scheme and love and hate as if they were ripped from history whole cloth. The Peacekeeper is suitable for young and old. At times, Hughes' writing reminds me of Umberto Ecco, at other times, Wallace Breen. With the Peacekeeper, Hughes delivers on the promise of earlier volumes, delivering a deeply-researched historical novel filled with mystery, adventure, romance, and command of his period so strong and effortless, so real, you'll think you've been to Roman Britain yourself! Few can equal Jess Steven Hughes. So come spend some time in Roman Britain with a gifted author whose skill is never obtrusive and whose characters you'll never forget. -- Janet Morris About the Author Jess Steven Hughes brought his lifetime's fascination with ancient Roman history into his debut novel, The Sign of the Eagle. The fascination continues as this has become part of a chain of books called the Britannia Romanus series. This includes The Wolf of Britannia, Part I and Part II. Another historical novel, The Broken Lance, set in Roman Britain and Imperial Rome is the first book of a duo-logy that includes The Peace Keeper. Jess is a retired a police detective sergeant, Long Beach Police Dept, Long Beach, CA. He holds a Masters Degree from the University of Southern California in Public Administration with a minor (my first academic love) in Ancient Mediterranean Civilizations. He also served four years United States Marine Corps (1962/66). As a retired person, Jess believes in keeping very busy. You must stay active mentally, physically and socially. These are a few of the keys to a long and healthy retirement. Writing novels has contributed greatly to my quality of life. He lives with his wife, Liz, on a four-acre mini-farm in Eastern Washington. His hobby is outdoor model railroading. He has an outdoor model railroad that was featured in the June/July 2010 issue of the regional magazine PRIME NORTHWEST (www.primenw.com). Check their website for the article. He was also featured in the Today segment of the Spokane Spokesman-Review, August 18, 2012, ﻿The Longest Chapter﻿, in which he discussed his quest to become a published author. Check the following link for the article. http: //www.spokesman.com/stories/2012/aug/18/the-longest-chapter/ Jess is a member of the Pacific Northwest Writers Association (PNWA) and is active in the Red Ink Fictioneers writers support group in the Spokane, WA area.

dialogue.user:
Thanks for the list! Let me take a look here. Well, my budget is between $15 and $30, so quite a few of these are either way too expensive or way too cheap. "PS I Love You" at $199 is definitely out of my range, and "To Sleep Gently" at $4.99 and "Untamed" at $6.14 are a bit under what I'd like to spend.

"Transcending Fire" at $23.95 sounds promising price-wise and it has a perfect 5.0 rating. And "An Amish Deception" at $12.99 is a bit under my budget but not too far off.

Could you tell me a bit more about **"Transcending Fire"** ? What's the story about? Is it more of a contemporary romance or supernatural?
dialogue.agent:
Here's the scoop on **"Transcending Fire"** :

**Price:** $23.95 | **Rating:** ⭐ 5.0/5.0 | **1 review so far**

It's a **fantasy/romance** hybrid, not contemporary. The story follows Alexandra, a warrior princess who gets captured and taken into enemy territory. She has to beguile a militant prince, outwit undead pirates, use forbidden necromancy magic, and unlock a long-forgotten power. One reviewer described it as having "steamy" romance and solid plot twists.

**Key detail from the review:** "The romance and the sex are perfect and steamy... plot is solid, and I enjoy the undead pirates — they were a nice touch... lots of great twists."

So this would be more of a **supernatural fantasy romance** with some darker, steamier elements. Does that sound like the kind of romance you're looking for, or would you prefer something more modern/contemporary? I can also look for other options in the $15-$30 range if this isn't quite your style!

result.title: Transcending Fire
result.features: Misfortune plagues a warrior princess who goes by the name Alexandra. She spent her youth commanding armies until the cruelest among her commanders turned on her in favor of an usurper masquerading as her cousin. Now, she is faced with a series of life-threatening challenges and one false step could mean the end of a reality that has run out of time. Transcending Fire is the first book in a series that is set in a fractured world that has been torn apart by a hundred year war. On her journey from the battlefield where she is captured and into the heart of an enemy empire she will beguile a militant prince, outwit a band of pirates, employ the use of forbidden necromancy magic and, with the help of a swamp witch, unlock a long forgotten power that was her birthright a hundred years ago.The message of this first book is to rise above insurmountable odds, even when your path is engulfed in flames. She was there the day the war began and ultimately she will bring an end to it.
